title: Prompt assembly: recipes & staged sandbox
content:
OVERVIEW:
This is a personal sandbox for assembling and stress-testing small "recipes" for chaining prompts and few-shot sets. Goal is practical: produce compact, robust templates that degrade gracefully when token budgets, temperature, or context length change. Keep experiments reproducible but lightweight — notes, failure modes, quick examples, and a short QA rubric.

GUIDING PRINCIPLES (working):
- Build templates as composable layers (instruction shell, constraints, example block, output schema).
- Keep mandatory instructions explicit and short; move heuristics to optional 'hints' block.
- Design for token-limited fallbacks: include a short fallback template for < 200 token context.
- Prefer deterministic anchors (explicit separators, labeled examples) to avoid role confusion.
- Track failure modes with short tags so we can triage later (degenerate-reply, hallucination, format-escape).

CURRENT EXPERIMENTS SUMMARY:
1) Dynamic Slot Assembly (DSA): assemble prompt from pieces at runtime so product can swap few-shots in/out depending on user persona.
- Positive: flexible, few-shots apply selectively.
- Failure: when examples are heterogeneous, model chooses an inconsistent style. Tag: style-drift.

2) Temperature Annealing Skeleton: meta-instruction that reduces temperature over iterative steps (e.g., brainstorm -> refine -> final).
- Use case: generate multiple candidate headlines then refine selected one with stricter temperature.
- Failure: sometimes early candidates include near-duplicates, wasting tokens. Tag: duplicate-candidate.

3) Prefix Cache Priming: preface with cached user-history summary (3 bullets) to keep context small.
- Works well for personalization; failure when cached summary is wrong/outdated -> wrong persona. Tag: wrong-context.

RECIPE: Product Copy Few-Shot (compact)
- Purpose: short, reliable ad copy generation for A/B tests.
- Token budget: 250 tokens max.
- Structure: SYSTEM_INSTR (one line) | CONSTRAINTS (bullets) | EXAMPLES (2 compact) | TASK_PROMPT | OUTPUT_SCHEMA

SYSTEM_INSTR:
You are a concise marketing writer. Output must be direct and benefit-driven.

CONSTRAINTS:
- <= 40 words per variant
- Mention primary benefit (faster, cheaper, safer)
- No technical jargon or claims of >100% improvements
- Tone: friendly but professional

EXAMPLES (compact few-shot):
-- Example 1 Input: "Calendar app" -> Output: "Never miss a meeting again — one-tap scheduling that syncs with your calendar. Try free for 14 days."
-- Example 2 Input: "File sync tool" -> Output: "Sync files across devices instantly with end-to-end encryption. Start syncing in minutes."

TASK_PROMPT:
Write three headline variants for: [PRODUCT_NAME] that focus on [PRIMARY_BENEFIT].

OUTPUT_SCHEMA:
- bullet list, 3 items, each a single sentence, no numbering, no commentary.

Notes: if output includes non-compliant text, re-run with 'strict-mode' by prepending: 'Enforce constraints: drop anything that violates constraints.'

FEW-SHOT BLOCK VARIANTS (experimental)
A) Homogeneous style examples (all imperative): reduces style-drift but might be repetitive.
B) Heterogeneous examples (imperative + descriptive): more creative, higher hallucination risk.

SAMPLE FAILURES (collected)
- degenerative-loop: model repeats same phrase across all variants when examples too similar.
- format-escape: model appends explanation like "(see more in docs)" outside schema.
- hallucinated-stat: claims speeds or numbers not provided.
- persona-bleed: earlier cached persona leaks into unrelated output.
- token-truncation: final line gets cut when example block is too long.

QA RUBRIC (quick manual checks)
- Compliance: Does it follow the output schema exactly? (Y/N)
- Benefit present: Is the primary benefit explicit? (Y/N)
- Tone check: friendly/professional? (Y/N)
- Jargon check: any technical words? (Y/N)
- Token estimate: approximate token count -> if near budget, run short-mode.

TESTING LOG (short)
2025-02-15: Ran Product Copy recipe with temp=0.7, 3 seeds. Observed duplicates; flagged duplicate-candidate.
2025-02-22: Switched to homogeneous examples, temp=0.5 -> better variety, fewer duplicates.
2025-02-28: Added fallback short-template for mobile UI (<= 20 words). Reduced truncation.

SHORT FALLBACK TEMPLATE (<=120 tokens)
System: "You are a brief copywriter. Keep outputs <= 20 words."
Prompt: "Write one headline for: [PRODUCT_NAME] focusing on [PRIMARY_BENEFIT]."
Output: single short line.

EDGE TESTS TO RUN (next iterations)
- Swap in a noisy cached-history to observe persona-bleed rates.
- Intentionally give contradictory examples to test guard rails.
- Vary available token budget: 100/200/400 and measure compliance rate.
- Run across model variants (ref-1.0, ref-1.1-q8, open-7b) to record behavior differences.

NOTES FOR INSTRUMENTATION / METRICS:
- Capture: prompt hash, model, temp, tokens_in, tokens_out, schema_violation(Y/N), failure_tags[].
- Quick metric: compliance_rate per 100 runs; baseline target >= 92% for production templates.

QUICK TODOs (priority order)
- [ ] Create test harness script to auto-run recipe across seeds + temps (Liam)
- [ ] Add strict-mode wrapper that strips examples if token budget < 180 (Riley)
- [ ] Document common failure tags and attach sample outputs to Confluence (Samir)
- [ ] Add fallback templates for >3 languages (stretch)

REFERENCES / LINKED NOTES
- See GH PR for modular few-shot loader: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-library/pull/87
- Idea: pair with Optimize signals (cache hit rate) to choose few-shot vs fallback at runtime.

RANDOM THOUGHTS / FUTURE: 
- Can we build a tiny classifier that predicts format-escape risk before sending full examples? (cheap proxy: check example diversity score)
- Consider signature tokens at example boundaries so degen loops can be detected early (e.g., insert unique marker between examples).

END OF SCRATCHPAD.
